description: Historical automated coaching before requested three-match rewrite. Contains corrected unsupported claims; rollback record, not an authoring template.

ea696257-4943-4784-805b-dedb3e74b1fa.headline: Objectives won this. The duo lane kept bleeding, and Greystone was a fucking wall.
ea696257-4943-4784-805b-dedb3e74b1fa.team: We gave up first blood and lost an early two-for-nothing in our own jungle, then took Mini Prime, won the five-on-five sequence as Fangtooth fell to us and kept taking objectives: Orb Prime, Primal Fangtooth, four towers and an inhibitor to their two towers. Six of seven won fights turned into a prize, which is how a game should get closed. Clean enough to win, sloppy enough to get punished by a better team.

focus.title: The duo lane needs a third body
focus.action: Both fights where only Drongo and Phase were credited on our side were lost, and the second came right before their only Fangtooth. Next game, the duo pulls in a third teammate before engaging near an objective. Check how many duo deaths land just before an enemy objective.

perPlayer.3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a: Greystone was the best player in the lobby, and it was not close. No deaths, the most damage mitigated on the team and our top hero damage on top of it: that is a frontline doing the whole fucking job. The standard to hold is simple. When Grux's stuns and Kwang's knockup are up, Greystone goes in first so that control lands on him, and Drongo and Gideon fight from behind him.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Kwang's Tainted Guard cuts the healing of anyone who basic-attacks him, so when Kwang is in the fight, Khaimera opens on Zinx or Argus and leaves Kwang to Greystone. That is the only adjustment. More objective damage than the other four combined, while dying less than his usual, is a jungler winning the game through the map rather than the scoreboard.
perPlayer.572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036: Gideon fought like a menace, then left the part that actually ends games to everyone else. Seven kills, two deaths and two clean skirmishes credited alongside Khaimera, then zero objective damage for the entire match. Not low. Zero. The kills were great; the towers and Primes never felt him. Next time he and Khaimera win a skirmish, Gideon follows onto the nearest objective or tower and shoots it until it falls.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Late game, when Kwang or Skylar has not shown on the map, Drongo rotates with Greystone beside him. The two sequences credited to just those two ended three for nothing and two for nothing. Two late deaths came outside any recorded fight, Kwang and Skylar collected them, and his hero damage sat well under his usual. With Greystone he won fights; away from any recorded fight he just died.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase did the support job on the map and gave too much away early. Twelve wards, all three of our ward clears and the team's biggest healing total are real work. Three early deaths, starting with first blood to Kwang, are not; that is less support and more delivery service. Until the ten-minute mark, Phase only trades forward when Khaimera is on our side of the map, and saves Phase Blink for the exit.

12.call: The kill sequence ended 5-1 with all five of us credited, and Fangtooth went to us in the same window. Kill credits place heroes in the fight; they do not show who started it.

17.7.call: Drongo and Greystone ended this sequence 3-0, while our Outer Tower fell in the same window with nobody of ours dead. The timing does not show which lane the tower was in or who could have defended it.

19.6.call: Gideon and Khaimera ended this sequence 3-0, but Fangtooth went to them in the same window after Phase and Drongo had both died. The order shows a trade; it does not prove the pit was contestable.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Duo lane: Phase with Drongo into Argus with Skylar, with Kwang taking first blood on Phase in that lane. Argus threatens from range with Dread Nova's stun and Ether Crystal's slow; Skylar finished Terminus lifesteal and Vanquisher. Across the team, Grux's Smash 'n Grab pull and stun and Kwang's Surge of the Heavens knockup can lock whichever ally Phase has linked.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Tainted Scepter has real targets here: it cuts healing on anything Phase hits with magical damage, which covers Skylar's Terminus lifesteal, the omnivamp from Kwang's Aura of the Heavens and Grux's own healing. Prophecy adds on-hit magical damage and attack speed to her basic attacks, a damage choice rather than protection. Galaxy Greaves gives both armors against a mixed enemy team. The final inventory does not show how often Blighted Spells actually landed.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Lotus rolls a random bonus on a timer and on takedowns. Flawless heals Phase and nearby allies when an ability hits an enemy hero, once per cast, which suits a heal-and-link plan. Prima Donna adds damage to heroes but makes Phase take more damage from every source; on a support with three early deaths, that is the trade to question. Immaculate, damage reduction while above 85% health, is the defensive option in the same slot.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Psychic Support makes Essence Catalyst restore mana to the linked ally. It helps a mana-hungry partner, but the record does not show who was linked or whether mana was ever short. Kindred Surge instead gives Hyperflux extra movement speed and health regeneration for its duration, a more direct escape and sustain tool for the duo once the ultimate is online.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Tranquility fits the job: Grace is a group heal with brief damage mitigation, and Visionary adds Solstone and a third ward slot. Phase placed more wards than her usual on the hero. The record does not show when Grace was cast or who was in range for it.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: Enra's Blessing, part of the recommended core, shields a nearby ally who gets immobilized, and this enemy team brought Grux's stuns, Kwang's knockup and Argus's stun. Taking it over Prophecy trades basic-attack damage for protection that triggers when that control lands on Drongo.

572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.matchup: Mid opponent: Zinx, built on Prophecy, Orion and Spectra, and the enemy's top hero damage dealer. Infuse heals allies, not Zinx, and Neural Regenesis can revive her or an ally, so burst her after it is spent. Grux and Kwang are the divers who can reach Gideon during Black Hole's channel: Grux with stuns, Kwang with a knockup.
572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.build: Soulbinder adds bonus damage to ability hits from long range and permanently grows Magical Power when it triggers, on a short cooldown. Truesilver Bracelet shields Gideon on ultimate cast and makes him immune to crowd control while the shield holds, a direct answer to Grux's stuns and Kwang's knockup during Black Hole. Oblivion Crown multiplies the power. Against the Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings core, this trades area burst for range and channel safety.
572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.eternal: Vesh adds damage over time to his ability damage on heroes. Tithe of Death returns mana and permanent ability haste on takedowns, a good fit for a mid who collects kills. Phylactery adds cooldown progression and a mana-scaled shield after the ultimate, stacking with Truesilver's shield on Black Hole. Mind Rot is the damage alternative, paid for with that second layer of post-ultimate protection.
572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.augment: Infinite Impact gives Void Breach unlimited range, and that pairs neatly with Soulbinder, whose bonus only triggers on ability hits from far away. It is a coherent long-range poke plan. Event Horizon is the alternative into the Grux and Kwang health pools: extra max-health damage in the centre of Cosmic Rift, traded for the cross-map Void Breach. The record cannot show how many long Void Breach hits landed.
572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.crest: Obelisk empowers a basic attack and builds Magical Power from souls when the target dies soon after. It suits a mid who gets takedowns, but it is a pure damage crest with no escape or protection attached. The record does not show the soul count or how often Condemn finished a target.
572a6e3b-9780-413a-9d7f-1f0da3ed1036.improvement: Keep the build. Two deaths do not point at a missing item, and Truesilver should stay while Grux's stuns and Kwang's knockup can reach Black Hole. If Zinx's magical damage starts forcing Gideon out of fights in a future game, a magical-armor item over Oblivion Crown trades raw power for survival. No inventory change touches objective damage.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Duo lane: Drongo with Phase into Skylar with Argus. Skylar finished Plasma Blade, Terminus and Vanquisher, so she brings lifesteal sustain and her own execute. Kwang ended on Tainted Guard, which bleeds and cuts the healing of anyone who basic-attacks him, so Drongo's damage on Kwang comes with a cost. Kwang and Skylar between them were credited with four of Drongo's five deaths.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Lightning Hawk gives a slowing empowered shot built from moving and attacking, Vanquisher adds physical penetration and executes heroes below 5% health, and Imperator raises critical damage. Drongo's Wastelander bleed applies on crits, so the crit path feeds his passive. That is the standard carry spine; the only recommended piece missing is Tainted Rounds.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when Drongo damages a hero below 30% health. Forage adds gold and XP per minion and monster kill, and Wind-Rider grants attack speed after a dash, which Pacifier's Adrenalize provides. The recommended pair is Dryad's Boon and Taproot. Natural Resistance is the safety alternative, a cleanse and tenacity below 25% health, traded for Forage income; it has a case into Grux's stuns and Kwang's knockup.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Shred Spree cuts Shrapnel Cannon's cooldown by 80% for half its damage, so the 30% physical armor shred comes up far more often. With four of our five heroes dealing physical damage, more frequent shred on Kwang and Grux helps the whole team, not just Drongo. The record does not show how often the shred connected.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Pacifier gives a short dash, an empowered physical hit that is much stronger below 20% health, and a recast after a kill. It is an aggressive crest whose dash can also be the exit. With two deaths away from any recorded fight, holding it as an escape is the safer default; the record does not show when it was used.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: Tainted Rounds over Imperator is the conditional swap: healing reduction on every basic hit against Skylar's Terminus lifesteal and the omnivamp from Kwang's aura, paid for with Imperator's extra critical damage. Take it when their carry or jungler is visibly healing through fights; skip it when nobody on their side sustains. Nothing in this match proves the current build lost a fight.

3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.matchup: Offlane opponent: Grux, a physical bruiser with Sky Splitter's current-health damage, Basilisk's armor shred and stuns from Smash 'n Grab and Warlord's Challenge. His healing makes anti-heal relevant, and he finished with the most deaths in the lobby. The team-level threat was different: Zinx was their top hero damage dealer, with Argus adding magical damage on top.
3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.build: Tainted Blade cuts healing on every physical hit, and his ability hits make a blighted target take more damage for a few seconds, a direct answer to Grux. Augmentation empowers a basic attack after each cast. Aegis of Agawar adds percentage physical and magical armor, doubled below 40% health, and Giant's Ring adds physical armor plus cooldown refunds when he is basic-attacked. Aegis's percentage bonus is the only magical defense, so no item adds flat magical armor into Zinx and Argus.
3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.eternal: Nihil grows Greystone's stats the longer he keeps damaging heroes, and every level-up or takedown permanently raises what that buff grants, which suits a frontline who stays in long fights. From the Abyss restores health during hero combat, and Adaptive Plating grants armor matching the damage type he takes, partly covering the magical side. It is the recommended pair and nothing in this match argues against it.
3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.augment: Imperial Soul makes Stone Forged Soul hit 12% harder over a 20% larger radius, so the stasis heal ends in a wider slam. That fits a frontline who wants to land the ultimate on several enemies at once. Tainted Oath is the anti-heal alternative, but Tainted Blade already covers that job.
3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.crest: Razorback adds both armors for a few seconds and reflects part of the damage he takes from heroes. Into a team that dives with Grux's stuns and Kwang's knockup, it is a sensible defensive crest. The record does not show when Echidna was active or how much it reflected.
3382512b-0b32-4920-9de6-dd2ba204849a.improvement: Keep the build: zero deaths says the defenses held. If Zinx's magical damage starts breaking him in a future game, Absolution over Giant's Ring adds magical armor and tenacity, plus mitigation and speed when he is immobilized, at the cost of Giant's Ring's physical armor and its cooldown refunds.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Jungle opponent: Kwang, built on Megacosm, Tainted Guard and Prophecy with the Aura of the Heavens omnivamp augment. Tainted Guard punishes basic attackers with a bleed and reduced healing, and Argus's Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical hits: two direct answers to Khaimera's regeneration-based sustain. Khaimera's credited kills were spread across Kwang, Zinx, Grux and Argus.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Ashbringer shortens non-ultimate cooldowns on every basic hit, more on crits. Claw of Hermes burns mana on hits, and its Magical Power adds extra Unleash attacks, since Unleash gains one per 30 Magical Power. Nuclear Rounds raises ability damage based on critical chance. It is an ability-amp skirmish build instead of the recommended Sky Splitter and Onixian Quiver core, and it carries no lifesteal item.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Exarch triggers when Khaimera heals or shields himself, granting attack speed and bonus magical on-hit damage for a few seconds. Revelation trims basic cooldowns on every cast, and Fervour heals him and nearby allies on hero hits. The pieces connect to a self-healing kit, but Exarch is built for supports, and enemy anti-heal shrinks the healing it rewards. The record does not show proc uptime.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Jungle Invasion adds physical power in the jungle and doubles it in the enemy jungle, rewarding a jungler who invades and fights on their side of the map. Feral Ambush, a longer leap, and Lane Lurker are the alternatives; nothing in this match makes a clear case for either over it.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Judgement deals area damage and heals on hero hits, with its cooldown shortening as he levels. It stacks with his regeneration and Fervour into a sustain package, and the same enemy anti-heal applies to it. The record does not show how many heroes each cast hit.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: Into Tainted Guard and Tainted Scepter, Onixian Quiver over Nuclear Rounds is the swap to compare: Onixia gives melee heroes 25% more total critical chance and 1% damage mitigation per 10% missing health, paid for with Nuclear Rounds' crit-scaled ability-damage boost. Keep the current build while Khaimera is clearing objectives this fast without dying much.

66b1d403-af84-4f1c-bf87-57e0c41df0ba.headline: Clean fucking stomp. We won the fights and then actually took the buildings.
66b1d403-af84-4f1c-bf87-57e0c41df0ba.team: We owned the early map: first blood, the first two Fangtooths and Mini Prime, then seven structures to their one, including two inhibitors. Won fights kept turning into objectives instead of highlight reels. The biggest leak was their Fangtooth, taken right after Murdock and Phase both died in a fight we still won; they also picked off a Seedling and one Outer Tower.

focus.title: Keep the duo alive for Fangtooth
focus.action: Next Fangtooth, count bodies before anyone walks in. If the carry and support are both down, the other three call contest or concede out loud, and a concede means hitting a tower somewhere else instead of a coin-flip at the pit.

perPlayer.78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c: DrabeyBaby was the best player in the lobby. Khaimera finished with twelve kills, the most hero damage of anyone in the match and most of our objective damage on top. He hit heroes, then hit buildings, which is the whole fucking job. The bare spot is vision: one ward placed, none cleared. If wards were equipped, switch to sentry next game and sweep the Fangtooth approach before calling the take.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Twice Murdock and Phase died in the same exchange, once in the lost fight during the Mini Prime window and once just before their Fangtooth. That is the main dent in a filthy game from Xeebs: first blood on Argus, twelve kills, damage well above the usual on the hero, and their duo dead five times before minute ten to our one. When Phase drops near an objective, Murdock backs off and regroups instead of taking the next trade.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Phase's job next game is simple: when Murdock commits, Mr_Meat31 stays behind him so the duo's healing outlasts the first burst. Dropping first in three fights and dying four times, above the usual on this hero, turns the healer into a spectator. Everything else was the job done: the most healing in the match and a hand in almost half our kills.
perPlayer.55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447: Destri never died and farmed well above the usual on Lt. Belica, then dealt hero damage well under it. The deathless part stays exactly as it is. When Khaimera or Murdock commits on a target, Belica throws the knockup and ult onto that same target from safe range. Farmed like a landlord, hit like a tenant; that follow-up is how the rent gets paid.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim played steady, low-drama Zarus: one death, farm above the usual, the full winning core finished. Steady is fine. Six takedowns out of our twenty-nine is the smallest share on the team, though, which is awfully polite for a hero who carries his own fucking arena. When we group for Fangtooth or an inhibitor push, Zarus walks in first beside Khaimera, or hits a tower elsewhere so they must split.

18.6.call: The sequence ended 3-2 for us. Murdock and Phase were our two deaths, and their Fangtooth fell within a minute; the order does not show whether we contested the pit.

20.7.call: The sequence ended 3-0 for us around the time their Outer and Inner Tower fell. Our only lost structure, an Outer Tower, fell inside the same window with nobody on our side dead.

22.4.call: The final sequence ended 4-0, and two enemy inhibitors fell shortly afterward. The match ended soon after with no further kills recorded.

78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c.matchup: Jungle opponent: Grux, an early-spiking engage bruiser with a pull-and-stun and a dragging charge, who finished Sky Splitter and Spectra, both basic-attack damage, and no defensive item. Gank targets were Legion and Argus in the duo lane and Aurora offlane. The whole-team threat to Khaimera's sustain is anti-heal: Aurora and Argus each finished Tainted Scepter, whose magical damage cuts healing by 45% for 4s on whoever it hits.
78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c.build: Sky Splitter's current-health damage and Ashbringer's cooldown reduction both trigger on successful basic attacks; Unleash speeds those hits up but applies on-hit effects at reduced effectiveness. Onixian Quiver's extra projectiles are ranged-only; on a melee hero it gives bonus critical chance and missing-health mitigation instead, and Imperator makes those crits hit harder. No enemy finished an armor item, so this damage met only base armor. The final inventory does not show when each piece came online.
78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c.eternal: Thraex marks the last hero Khaimera basic-attacked, raising his damage against them and trimming theirs against him. Savage Strikes adds on-hit damage that ramps against heroes and heals for it; Ferocity stacks attack speed the longer hero combat lasts. All three reward sticking to one target, which is his kit. The healing piece runs into two Tainted Scepters; Golden Mane, less damage from non-AoE hits, is the slot-two alternative at the cost of Ferocity's attack speed.
78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c.augment: Feral Ambush adds 10% range to Ambush, the leap that opens his combo. That is engage reach, not damage. Jungle Invasion is the alternative: physical power in the jungle, doubled in the enemy jungle, which only beats extra leap range when invading is the plan. The record cannot show how many entries the extra range enabled, so there is no basis to call either the better pick here.
78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c.crest: Eviscerator's active adds attack speed, omnivamp and empowered basic attacks for 6s, the same stick-to-one-target pattern as the items. The omnivamp half loses value whenever Aurora's or Argus's Tainted Scepter is on him. It fits as a follow-up once Khaimera is committed, not as an opener from range. Activation timing is not recorded.
78c58fb9-a3cb-44bd-99e5-9a08a16ece1c.improvement: Keep the core. Twelve kills and the team's biggest objective damage do not ask for a rebuild. If magical damage starts ending his entries, compare Absolution against Imperator: magical armor, tenacity and a mitigation burst when immobilized, versus extra critical damage. In this match his three deaths came to Aurora, Legion and Grux, so no single damage type proves the swap yet.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Duo lane: Murdock with Phase into Legion with Argus. Legion finished Malady, which rewards hitting low-health targets, and Infernum, a max-health burn that ignites after repeated hits; Argus pokes from range with a stun and a slowing crystal. The enemy duo died five times before minute ten to our one, and first blood was Murdock's on Argus. Of Murdock's three deaths, Argus got two and Grux one.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Lightning Hawk builds Momentum while moving or attacking for an empowered, slowing shot; Vanquisher adds physical penetration and executes heroes under 5% health; Imperator makes critical strikes deal 30% more. This is the exact winning core. No enemy finished an armor item, so penetration met base armor only. On core, no build impact proven in this match.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Vermis adds max-health damage on every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero within 2.5s, and Serration adds missing-health damage to that proc. Melting Point needs targets above 125 physical armor, and no enemy finished an armor item, so that slot had little to bite on. Sub-Surface, 7% less damage from AoE abilities, is the slot-two alternative into Iggy & Scorch's fire zones, giving up damage on heavily armored targets this lobby never built.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Justice's Reach makes Shots Fired, the empowered long-range attack after five landed basics, pierce units and gain 250 range. That lets the shot reach through a minion wave from a safer distance. Martial Law, more ult damage and gold on hero kills, is the alternative in a game that snowballs like this one. Neither is proven better by this record.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Pacifier dashes and empowers the next physical hit, deals 2.5x damage below 20% health and can be recast after a kill within 3s. It stacks well with Vanquisher's execute threshold for finishing. The dash is also Murdock's only extra mobility beyond Hot Pursuit, so spending it on a chase spends the exit. Use and resets are not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: Keep the core and the augment. The cheapest test is Sub-Surface for Melting Point, since nobody on their side built armor. Argus, a magical damage dealer, got two of Murdock's three deaths; if that pattern repeats, compare Dread against Imperator: magical armor and a magical-damage block versus extra critical damage.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Duo lane: Phase with Murdock into Argus with Legion. Argus pokes from range and stuns with Dread Nova; Legion's Malady punishes targets under 40% health, so Phase's heals matter most before Murdock drops that low. Aurora and Argus both finished Tainted Scepter, which cuts healing on anyone their magical damage hits, including whoever Phase is healing.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Prophecy adds magical on-hit damage to basic attacks and Tainted Scepter adds anti-heal on magical damage plus a stacking bonus on ability hits, a damage-leaning support build in place of the Marshal, Enra's Blessing and Galaxy Greaves core. The enemy had no healer; Grux's 13376 healing was the biggest enemy sustain that anti-heal could cut. Nothing in this match shows the missing core would have changed a fight.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Lotus rolls a small random bonus every two minutes and on takedowns. Flawless heals Phase and nearby allies when an ability hits an enemy hero, once per cast, on top of her passive heal; Fragrance adds magical damage only at close range. The field on Phase mostly runs Exarch, whose heal-triggered attack speed and magical on-hit would land on a Linked Murdock, at the cost of Lotus's stacking bonuses.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Psychic Support adds a mana restore for the Linked ally through Essence Catalyst, per its catalog text. It only pays when the Linked carry is short on mana, which this record cannot show. Kindred Surge, the more common pick on Phase, adds movement speed and health regen during Hyperflux and suits a duo that needs to escape dives. Final Flash trades Energy Lance length for damage.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Tranquility heals Phase and nearby heroes and adds brief damage mitigation, and its passive raises the ward cap to three. The heal only reaches allies in range when it is pressed. The ward cap is the part to use harder: eight placements sat below the usual for this player on Phase. Activation timing is not recorded.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: Keep the damage-leaning pair while the enemy has no healer and Phase is landing ability hits. If Aurora's root-and-stun chain or Grux's pull-and-stun starts landing on Murdock, compare Enra's Blessing against Prophecy: a shield on immobilized allies in range versus basic-attack damage. Magical armor is the other conditional slot, since three of their five dealt magical damage and none of us built it; Devotion trades Prophecy's damage for that.

55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447.matchup: Midlane: Lt. Belica into Iggy & Scorch, a zone-control mage who burns through fire zones and a turret and was their top hero damage. He finished Azure Core, Claw of Hermes and Wraith Leggings; Claw of Hermes drains mana on basic attacks and Wraith Leggings adds damage to heroes under 40% health. Belica's drone drains mana and her ult scales with missing mana, so this was a mana fight on both sides.
55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447.build: Orb of Enlightenment scales with level and restores a little missing health on each cast. Noxia marks a hero with one ability and pops max-health damage when a second ability hits. Megacosm adds max-health and bonus-health damage over time. Together they reward a two-ability rotation, where the winning core of Combustion and Wraith Leggings leans on burst. Aurora, Argus and Iggy & Scorch all finished health items, so Megacosm's second half had targets. The inventory alone does not explain the damage gap.
55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447.eternal: Lotus rolls a small random bonus every two minutes and on takedowns. Early Bloom grants an extra level at twelve, which pairs with Combat Veteran's passive experience into a leveling plan. Fragrance adds magical damage to heroes within 800 units, which asks an immobile mage to stand close. Masterpiece, stacking damage and speed on kills, is the slot-one alternative when Belica is the one finishing takedowns, at the cost of the bonus level.
55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447.augment: Combat Veteran gives movement speed and passive experience: a level-lead plan with no direct combat effect. Devastating Bombs, more Void Bomb damage on isolated targets, and Pulsefire Rounds, magical on-hit damage on basic attacks, put that slot into fights instead. With damage well under the usual on the hero, a combat augment is the next thing to test, not a proven fix.
55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447.crest: Epoch is a short stasis on a long cooldown, a pure survival button with no damage. Belica finished deathless; the record does not show whether it was ever pressed. Keep it while the enemy brings a diving jungler with a pull-and-stun and Aurora's frost chain, since an immobile mage needs one escape.
55ce8bb7-8577-43b5-a6ea-a62219fa5447.improvement: Keep Noxia and Epoch. If damage again lands well under the usual, compare Combustion against Orb of Enlightenment first: burst on ability damage versus level-scaled power, health and a small heal per cast. If Iggy & Scorch's magical damage is what forces Belica out of range, Spellbreaker brings magical armor and a spell shield in place of a damage slot such as Megacosm.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Offlane: Zarus into Aurora, a control tank who chains slow, root and stun. Aurora finished Magnify, Tainted Scepter and Prophecy: magical-armor shred on ability hits, anti-heal on her magical damage and on-hit damage. That anti-heal lands directly on Zarus's lifesteal plan. Aurora scored the only kill on Zarus in the match.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Augmentation empowers the next basic after each ability cast, Mutilator turns basic attacks and ability hits into max-health damage plus omnivamp, and Basilisk shreds physical armor on every hero hit, stacking to six. All three reward staying in contact, which is what Coliseum is for. The enemy finished no armor item, so the shred worked on base armor. This is the full winning core; no build impact proven in this match.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Marrow heals off hero damage, more as Zarus's health drops. Leech cuts base health regen of enemies within 550 units, and Roses adds takedown gold and a stronger Marrow heal after hero kills. Both ask Zarus to be in the middle of fights and finishing them. Two enemy Tainted Scepters cut every Marrow heal they touch; Jealousy, more damage as health falls, is the slot-two alternative that does not depend on healing, at the cost of Roses' gold.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Master Of Spears softens the cooldown penalty when Spear Of Nyr is thrown rather than thrust, so it pays when Zarus throws the spear for its bonus damage on low-health targets. Flow State, a shorter Evade cooldown that resets on takedowns, is the dive-and-reset alternative. The record cannot show how often the spear was thrown, so neither is proven better here.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Soulbearer is a mage crest. Its mana does little for Zarus and its magical power only feeds Spear of Nyr and Evade's smaller scalings; ability haste and the active's shield and speed are what he uses. Brutallax, a fighter crest, trades those for physical power, health and omnivamp, plus a cleanse and tenacity that basic attacks extend, answering Aurora's root-and-stun chain directly.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: Swap the crest first: Brutallax over Soulbearer gives stats Zarus scales with and a cleanse into Aurora's control, sacrificing a shield and movement burst. Keep the item core. If magical damage starts deciding his fights, Legacy offers magical armor, tenacity and a cleanse with immunity below 40% health, at the cost of a damage slot such as Basilisk.

0be308cb-4508-4daf-98ef-9fc53ced79b8.headline: Drongo ran their duo lane like a fucking turnstile. We never lost a fight and still left two wins unspent.
0be308cb-4508-4daf-98ef-9fc53ced79b8.team: This was a stomp built on the duo lane. Drongo and Phase gave up nothing early while Kira died three times, and the team did not lose a single fight after that. We took two of three Fangtooths and four towers to their one. Their first Fangtooth came with Belica dead, and Mini Prime went to them with all five of us alive.

focus.title: Win the fight, hit the tower
focus.evidence: Two of our five won fights had no tower or objective follow within 90 seconds. The other three were followed by a structure or a Fangtooth.
focus.action: After any won fight with nothing major up, the living laners walk to the nearest enemy tower before anyone backs, and one player names that tower in voice. Next game, count how many won fights end in a structure or objective.

perPlayer.dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5: Best player in the lobby, and it was not close. Drongo treated Kira like a respawn timer with legs, killing her six times and Ikra five, and lived through every fight but the last. That is the standard, not a lucky night. His one death came to Greystone in the final fight, so when Greystone commits onto him, Drongo backs toward Steel and fights from behind him.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Clean support game. Zero deaths, a hand in 83% of our kills, and heals flowing behind a carry who died once all game. Vision is the soft spot: eight wards, below her usual Phase count. Next game, when an enemy objective is about to spawn and we are not trading elsewhere, Phase calls the group to the pit and spends her vision there before they arrive.
perPlayer.8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e: Khaimera hit objectives like they owed him money, with the team's top objective damage and kill credits in three of our won fights. The early game was messier. He died twice before the first big fight, to Greystone and then Scarlett, both outside any team fight. Before an early gank or invade, Khaimera calls the target and waits for the laner to confirm; if Greystone's whereabouts are unknown, take the camp and skip the duel.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Argus got both of Belica's deaths, and the first one, outside any fight, came right before their first Fangtooth. So in the minute before a Fangtooth spawns, Belica shoves the wave and walks to the pit with Khaimera, so Argus never gets her alone. The rest was sharp: farm well above her usual pace and kills in three of our won fights, two on Argus.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Four enemy towers fell and Steel did not put a single fucking point of damage on any of them. When we win a fight and an enemy tower is in reach, Steel walks in first, takes the tower shots and hits it. The frontline job itself was done: the most damage mitigated on our team, a kill on Scarlett, and only two deaths, both to Scarlett.

13.9.call: The kill sequence ended 4-1, with Drongo credited on all four kills. Mini Prime fell to them in the same window while we took Fangtooth and an Outer Tower.

19.7.call: The kill sequence ended 4-0. Their Inner Tower fell inside it, then an Outer Tower and our second Fangtooth followed.

21.9.call: The final kill sequence ended 4-2, with Drongo and Khaimera the two deaths. Another enemy Outer Tower fell afterward, and the match ended soon after that.

dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5.matchup: Duo lane was Drongo with Phase into Kira with Ikra. Kira's Solaris heals her for half the damage of each empowered basic attack, and Ruination drains mana with a true-damage bleed; Ikra built Combustion and Astral Catalyst for ability burst. Neither enemy duo player finished an armor item. Across the map, Greystone was the bigger sustain problem, healing 16,390 over the game, and Argus brought the main magic damage.
dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5.build: Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator form a crit package: Imperator makes critical strikes hit harder, Vanquisher executes heroes below 5% health, and Lightning Hawk empowers a slowing shot after enough movement and attacks. Demolisher took the slot the common core gives Tainted Rounds. Its first passive ignores a quarter of physical armor on everyone; its second only bites on bonus armor, and nobody on their side finished an armor item. The final list is not purchase order, so which items were online in each fight is unknown.
dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5.eternal: Weald fires true-damage projectiles when Drongo damages a hero below 30% health, once per hero every ten seconds, which suits a carry who finishes fights. Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill. Wind-Rider grants attack speed after a dash, and Pacifier's active is a dash, so the two can chain on paper; whether that lined up is not recorded. The recommended pairing is Dryad's Boon with Taproot, trading Forage's farm and post-dash attack speed for basic-ability cooldown cuts and on-hit healing.
dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5.augment: Bring The Boom makes Rad Rounds splash 60% of its eruption damage onto nearby enemies, which pays off when fights bunch up, and it is the usual Drongo pick. Shred Spree trades half of Shrapnel Cannon's damage for a far shorter cooldown on its armor shred; with no enemy armor items in this lobby, that shred had less to work on. Keep Bring The Boom.
dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5.crest: Pacifier dashes and empowers the next physical hit with bonus damage that rises 2.5 times against targets below 20% health, and a hero kill within three seconds allows a recast. That suits a carry who finished thirteen kills, though resets and dash usage are not in the record. Keep it.
dba6b55f-c3aa-499a-aa76-266f3f9610d5.improvement: Keep the build. Tainted Rounds in Demolisher's slot would put healing reduction on every basic attack, but Phase's Tainted Scepter and Steel's Tainted Guard already carried anti-heal against Greystone here. It becomes the swap only when nobody else on our side buys healing reduction and the enemy jungler or carry heals heavily; it gives up some physical power and Demolisher's armor ignore.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Support lane was Phase with Drongo into Ikra with Kira. Ikra's Astral Catalyst adds bonus damage against shielded targets, which matters little against Phase, whose kit heals rather than shields. Combustion gives Ikra area burst when her abilities land; Phase's stacking Essence Catalyst heals answer that over time rather than prevent it.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Prophecy adds magical on-hit damage and attack speed to Phase's own basic attacks. Tainted Scepter puts healing reduction on anyone her magical damage touches, the right tool against Greystone's heavy healing. Galaxy Greaves adds both armors. The common core runs Marshal and Enra's Blessing instead, buffing nearby allies' attack speed and shielding immobilized allies. Phase chose personal damage plus anti-heal over ally utility. The record cannot show how often the anti-heal was applied.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Exarch's major gives a healed target 10% attack speed and magical on-hit damage for four seconds. Essence Catalyst heals Phase and her linked ally after every ability cast, so a linked Drongo can receive that buff often, though uptime is not recorded. Preservation boosts healing Phase receives; Fervour heals nearby allies when she basic attacks heroes, which pairs with Prophecy. Revelation would trade Preservation's self-sustain for faster basic cooldowns and more Essence Catalyst triggers; with zero deaths, self-sustain was not the bottleneck.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Psychic Support makes Essence Catalyst also restore the linked ally's missing mana. That helps a mana-hungry carry stay in long fights, but nothing here shows Drongo running dry. The more common Kindred Surge adds movement speed and health regeneration to Hyperflux for both linked heroes, trading mana sustain for a faster chase or escape. Either fits; nothing here forces a swap.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Tranquility's active heals Phase and nearby heroes and grants brief damage mitigation, and the crest raises the ward cap from two to three. That extra slot only pays if it is filled before objectives spawn. Whether the cap was ever full is not recorded.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: Keep Tainted Scepter whenever the enemy jungler or carry heals heavily, as Greystone did here with 16390 healing. If a future enemy instead locks down our carry with stuns and roots, Enra's Blessing in Prophecy's slot shields immobilized allies nearby; it trades Phase's own on-hit damage and attack speed for protection she cannot otherwise provide. Nothing in this match proves that swap was needed.

8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e.matchup: Jungle matchup was Khaimera into Greystone, who built Overlord, Augmentation and Basilisk and healed 16,390 over the game. Greystone killed Khaimera twice; Khaimera killed him once. His other kill credits went to Argus twice and Ikra once. Scarlett's Mutilator deals max-health damage on hits, which matters for a jungler stacking health.
8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e.build: Overlord deals health-scaled on-hit damage with cleave and grows Khaimera's health on kills. Basilisk shreds physical armor with stacks on every hero hit, and Draconum boosts healing while fighting and heals on takedowns. That is a drain-tank package rather than the attack-speed core of Sky Splitter, Ashbringer and Onixian Quiver. Nobody on their side bought armor, so Basilisk only shred base armor. The build still sat behind the team's top objective damage; that proves farm and pressure, not which item mattered.
8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e.eternal: Lotus grants a random small bonus every two minutes and every takedown. Early Bloom adds a level on reaching level twelve, and Immaculate cuts damage by 10% only above 85% health. Khaimera absorbed the most damage on our team, and Immaculate stops working once health drops below that line, so its value in long fights is limited. Masterpiece with Prima Donna is the common Khaimera Lotus pairing: kill-stacking damage and a flat damage boost, paid for with 6% more damage taken.
8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e.augment: Feral Ambush adds 10% range to Ambush, his gap-closing leap, which helps start ganks from farther out. Jungle Invasion adds physical power in the jungle, doubled in the enemy jungle; one of our won fights happened deep in their half, so it is a draft-time option when the plan is to invade. It gives up the longer engage range. Feral Ambush is the common pick and a fine keep.
8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e.crest: Iceskorn Talons drops an ice sheet that gives allies on it physical power and movement speed and slows enemies on it. With Drongo as the main physical damage dealer, it fits grouped fights better than solo duels. Whether allies stood on the sheet is not recorded.
8d51b81b-7acf-4747-8b3a-2a225758fb5e.improvement: No forced swap. If the next lobby again has no armor buyers, compare Sky Splitter's current-health on-hit and lifesteal against Basilisk: it trades Basilisk's health and armor shred for attack speed and sustain. If Greystone's healing drags a duel out, Khaimera owns no anti-heal; that job sat with Phase's Tainted Scepter and Steel's Tainted Guard here, so coordinate it rather than duplicating it.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Mid matchup was Belica into Argus, a mage who built Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings. Azure Core gives Argus a large mana pool and a shield below 40% health, which matters because Void Drone drains current mana and Neural Disruptor hits harder against missing mana. The kill trade was even at two each, and both of Belica's deaths came from Argus. Greystone and Kira were her later targets in team fights.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Combustion deals area burst when Belica's abilities hit, with its cooldown shortened by hero damage, and Noxia marks heroes hit by one ability so a second ability adds 6% of their max health. Belica's kit layers Void Bomb, Seismic Assault and the drone, so the mark is easy to set up in principle. The missing core piece is Wraith Leggings, which is magical penetration and bonus damage on low-health heroes, not defense. Only two finished items show, and purchase timing is unknown.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Aion's major gives mana regeneration on casts and gold equal to 6% of spell damage dealt to heroes. Bottomless Vial pays off whenever she takes a River Buff, and our team took most river objectives in this match. Runic Focus scales magical power with current mana, which suits Void Bomb's mana return on hits. Philosopher in Bottomless Vial's slot is the steadier gold option if Belica is not the one taking river buffs. Who took each river buff is not recorded.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Combat Veteran adds movement speed and passive experience over time, an economy pick. Devastating Bombs adds 15% Void Bomb damage against isolated targets and suits hunting a lone Argus; Pulsefire Rounds adds damage to basic attacks. Both of Belica's Argus kills came inside won fights, so nothing here shows another augment would have changed the result. Keep it.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Soulbearer gives a shield scaled by magical power and mana, plus magical lifesteal and movement speed for eight seconds. It fits the Runic Focus mana plan and is Belica's main answer to an Argus all-in. Whether it was used before either death is not recorded.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: Wraith Leggings is the natural third item when fights end with enemies low. If Argus keeps being the one who ends Belica's life, a defensive third slot outranks more penetration; the trade is less kill pressure for a longer life in lane. Two deaths alone do not decide which problem comes first, so make the call from the next lane, not this one.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Offlane matchup was Steel into Scarlett, who built Mutilator, Infernum and The Perforator. Mutilator deals max-health damage on hits, The Perforator ignores 30% of physical armor, and Infernum's ignite deals more damage for every point of bonus armor on its target. Scarlett killed Steel twice and Steel killed Scarlett once. Greystone, the other physical bruiser, also healed heavily.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Fire Blossom burns nearby enemies with damage that ramps the longer it sticks, and Tainted Guard puts healing reduction and a bleed on anyone who basic attacks Steel. Against Greystone's healing, Tainted Guard has a clear trigger. Both items stack bonus armor, though, and Infernum turns bonus armor into extra ignite damage. Flux Matrix, the missing core piece, adds magical armor and makes nearby enemies take more magic damage.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Krix grows maximum health with level. Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after eight seconds without hero damage, and Cannibalism adds permanent health on takedowns, a lane-sustain setup. Voracity is the farming alternative, restoring health and gold on unit kills. Festering Wounds would make Steel's stuns and knockups cut enemy healing, giving up Regenerative Tissue's recovery between trades for anti-heal on Greystone and Scarlett.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Heavy Metal turns Steel's total armor into bonus magical damage on Heavy Punches and Shield Bash, so the armor items do double duty. It is the standard Steel pick. Keep it.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Razorback's active adds 20% to both armors for five seconds and reflects 15% of incoming hero damage as true damage. That suits a trade with Scarlett, who has to hit Steel to deal her damage. Whether the active was used before either death is not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: Keep Tainted Guard while a heavy healer like Greystone is basic attacking Steel. The conditional change is the next item. Each extra point of bonus armor also feeds Scarlett's Infernum ignite, so Flux Matrix or another health and magic-armor piece balances Steel against Argus and Ikra too. It gives up some physical sturdiness against Scarlett and Greystone.
